newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin sets one-yr bond auction for July 22.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin sets one-yr bond auction for July 22.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry will auction an unspecified tranche of one-year state bonds on July 22, the central bank (NBS) said in a statement on Wednesday.
The bonds, which have a nominal value of 100,000 crowns, carry a fixed annual coupon rate of 11.00 percent.

Average yield in the last auction of one-year state bonds on July 8 rose to 16.812 percent, from 15.868 percent in the previous succesful auction on May 27. The ministry rejected all bids on June 17 due to the high yield demanded.

The ministry has held seven auctions of one-year state bonds this year -- four of which were succesful -- offering a fixed interest rate of 10.00 percent in the first six auctions and a 11.00 percent coupon in the last auction.
The ministry does not set an amount on offer at state securities auctions, nor does it set a minimum or maximum limit price on bids.

It uses T-bills and state bonds as the main tools to cover the state budget deficit, which widened to 7.177 billion crowns in the January-May period of 1997 from a shortfall of 4.692 billion crowns for the first four months of this year.
